qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Groupe ADP operates an unreplicable infrastructure monopoly across the Greater Paris air basin (Paris-CDG, Paris-Orly, and Le Bourget). Physical runway slot scarcity and environmental restrictions prevent competing hub development. Under its dual-till regulatory model, non-aeronautical retail (Extime Paris luxury duty-free JV with Lagardère) exercises exceptional unregulated pricing power over high-spending intercontinental travelers, while aeronautical charges adjust via economic regulation agreements.
qualitative.note: Rejected at Gate 5 (Management & Capital Allocation, Score = 0). Paris CDG and Orly are irreplaceable national infrastructure assets, but Groupe ADP is 50.6% owned by the French State and suffers from acute capital allocation and governance pathologies: recurring regulatory conflict with ART over allowed aeronautical charges, bureaucratic inertia, and value-destructive international M&A (GMR Airports in India, TAV in Turkey) that loaded the balance sheet with €8.57B in net debt (>13x net income) and caused large impairment charges (€330M in 2024).
qualitative.evidence: State-dominated corporate governance has directed massive capital into speculative overseas airport stakes (GMR in India, TAV in Turkey) instead of disciplined per-share compounding. Net financial debt reached €8.57B at year-end 2024 against normalized net income of €638M (and reported net income of €342M, hit by a €330M merger charge on Indian assets), depressing consolidated ROIC to ~5-7%.
